day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Barcelona El Prat Airport at 19:20. Take the Aerobus (€6.75 one-way) or the L9 Sud metro line (€5.15 with T-Casual card) to the city, then connect to Sant Just Desvern via bus L60 or taxi. Check in to Sercotel Porta Barcelona. Once settled, take a short stroll around the Sant Just Desvern neighbourhood to get your bearings and grab a casual dinner nearby.

meals.lunch: N/A – on the plane or airport
meals.dinner: Bar-restaurant near the hotel in Sant Just Desvern – look for a local 'menú del día' (evening version) or a neighbourhood tapas bar. Budget €8–12 for a simple set meal with a drink.

day_by_day.notes: Buy a T-Casual 10-trip metro/bus card (€12.15) at the airport – it covers all public transport within Zone 1 and will save money throughout the trip. Keep the first night light; jet lag and travel fatigue are real. The hotel is in the suburban municipality of Sant Just Desvern, about 8 km southwest of central Barcelona, well connected by bus and metro.

day_by_day.morning: Head into central Barcelona via bus L60 + Metro L3 (Zona Universitària). Start the day at Parc Güell (free to walk the monumental zone perimeter and forested paths; ticketed monumental zone ~€10 – book online in advance to save queuing). Arrive early (09:00) to beat the heat and crowds. Explore Gaudí's mosaic terraces, viaducts, and panoramic city views. Spend 1.5–2 hours here.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take the metro down to the Eixample district. Visit the exterior of Casa Batlló and Casa Milà (La Pedrera) on Passeig de Gràcia – both are stunning from the street for free. Duck into the Bloc de la Discòrdia block to admire Casa Amatller and Casa Lleó Morera facades at no cost. Grab lunch in the Eixample, then visit the interior courtyard of the Universitat de Barcelona (free, beautiful neo-Gothic architecture). Cool off in a café during the hottest part of the afternoon (14:00–16:30).
day_by_day.evening: Sagrada Família Guided Tour – book the evening slot (around 17:00–18:30) to avoid peak midday heat. The guided tour reveals the intricate symbolism of Gaudí's unfinished basilica; tickets with tower access ~€26–32 (book online in advance). Afterwards, explore the surrounding Eixample streets. For nightlife, head to the Gràcia neighbourhood (a short walk north) – lively plazas like Plaça del Sol and Plaça de la Vila de Gràcia fill up with locals from 21:00 onwards. Enjoy cheap cañas (draft beer ~€2–3) at outdoor terrace bars.

meals.breakfast: Café or bakery near the hotel or at a bar in the Zona Universitària area – coffee and a croissant or tostada con tomate for €3–5.
meals.lunch: Menú del día in the Eixample – a 3-course lunch with bread and a drink for €12–14. Look for restaurants one block off Passeig de Gràcia for better value.
meals.dinner: Tapas and pintxos in Gràcia neighbourhood – order patatas bravas, pan con tomate, and croquetas. Budget €10–15 per person including drinks.

day_by_day.notes: August heat peaks between 13:00–17:00 (avg high ~29°C) – plan indoor or shaded activities during this window. Carry a reusable water bottle; public drinking fountains (fonts) are plentiful across Barcelona. Book Sagrada Família tickets online at least a few days ahead – they sell out fast in August.

day_by_day.morning: Take the metro to Barceloneta (L4, Barceloneta stop). Spend the morning at Barceloneta Beach – free and one of the most iconic urban beaches in Europe. Swim, people-watch, and enjoy the Mediterranean. Walk the Passeig Marítim promenade northward toward Port Olímpic. Visit the striking Frank Gehry 'Peix' (Fish) sculpture and the Port Olímpic marina area (free to admire).
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to El Born / Sant Pere neighbourhood (short walk or metro). Explore the Barri Gòtic (Gothic Quarter) on foot – completely free. Wander through Carrer del Bisbe, Plaça de Sant Jaume, the Roman Temple of Augustus (free exterior, small fee inside ~€2.50), and the medieval lanes. Visit the Basílica de Santa Maria del Mar (free entry, small donation appreciated) – a stunning 14th-century Gothic church, arguably more atmospheric than the Cathedral. Browse the El Born market building (free to enter, Roman ruins visible inside).
day_by_day.evening: Palau de la Música Catalana Evening Concert – attend a live performance at this UNESCO World Heritage modernista masterpiece designed by Lluís Domènech i Montaner. Budget tickets start from €18–35 depending on the programme; check the official website for the August schedule and book in advance. The stained-glass skylight and ornate interior are breathtaking, especially lit up during a concert. Afterwards, the El Born neighbourhood comes alive at night – enjoy a nightcap at one of the many cocktail bars on Carrer del Rec or Passeig del Born (cocktails from €7–9).

meals.breakfast: Chiringuito (beach bar) breakfast at Barceloneta – coffee and a bocadillo or tostada for €4–6, or grab supplies from a nearby Mercadona supermarket for even less.
meals.lunch: Mercat de Santa Caterina (less touristy alternative to La Boqueria) – pick up fresh fruit, cheese, cured meats, and bread for a self-assembled picnic lunch for €6–8.
meals.dinner: Pre-concert early dinner in El Born – try a set menú or a bocadillo bar. Alternatively, eat a larger lunch and have pintxos before the concert for €8–12.

day_by_day.notes: La Boqueria market on Las Ramblas is very touristy and overpriced – Mercat de Santa Caterina or Mercat de l'Abaceria in Gràcia offer the same experience at local prices. Avoid carrying valuables on Las Ramblas – pickpocketing is common. The Palau de la Música has a smart-casual dress code; avoid beachwear.

day_by_day.morning: Take the metro or FGC train to Montjuïc. Ride the Telefèric de Montjuïc cable car (€12.70 return) or hike up for free via the gardens path. Visit the Castell de Montjuïc (€5 entry, free on first Sunday of the month) for panoramic views over the city and port. Explore the surrounding Jardins de Laribal and Jardí Botànic de Barcelona (€3.50) – beautifully landscaped and far less crowded than central attractions.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend to the Poble Sec neighbourhood at the foot of Montjuïc – one of Barcelona's most authentic and affordable barrios. Visit the Pavelló Mies van der Rohe (Barcelona Pavilion) – a landmark of modernist architecture (€5 entry). Walk along Avinguda del Paral·lel. In the late afternoon, explore the Raval neighbourhood – visit the MACBA (Museum of Contemporary Art Barcelona) courtyard and plaza (free to sit and watch skaters), and the CCCB cultural centre (some exhibitions free). Browse the colourful street art in the area.
day_by_day.evening: Poble Sec is home to the famous Carrer de Blai – the 'pintxos street' of Barcelona, lined with bars offering pintxos from €1–1.50 each. This is a perfect budget dinner and social experience. Afterwards, explore Barcelona's nightlife: the Raval and El Poble Sec areas have excellent, affordable bars. For clubs, Sala Apolo on Carrer Nou de la Rambla is a legendary venue with affordable entry (€10–15) and great live music or DJ nights. Clubs in Barcelona typically don't fill up until 01:00–02:00.

meals.breakfast: Café in Poble Sec or pack a breakfast from a supermarket – coffee and a pastry for €2–4.
meals.lunch: Menú del día in Poble Sec – this neighbourhood has excellent value restaurants. Budget €11–13 for a full 3-course lunch with drink.
meals.dinner: Carrer de Blai pintxos crawl – eat your fill for €10–15 including a couple of drinks. Arrive around 20:00–21:00 for the freshest pintxos.

day_by_day.notes: Montjuïc is very exposed and hot in August – bring sunscreen, a hat, and plenty of water. The Telefèric cable car can have long queues; consider going early or taking the Funicular de Montjuïc from Paral·lel metro station (covered by your T-Casual card). Barcelona nightlife runs very late – if you plan to go clubbing, take a siesta in the afternoon.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning – visit the Sagrada Família neighbourhood surroundings if you want more photos in the morning light (exterior is free to photograph from the street). Alternatively, take the metro to Diagonal and walk through the upscale Pedralbes neighbourhood to see the Palau Reial de Pedralbes gardens (free entry) and the Monestir de Pedralbes (€5 entry) – a beautifully preserved 14th-century Gothic monastery that is one of Barcelona's most underrated gems.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the Eixample for last-minute souvenir shopping at affordable spots – avoid tourist shops on Las Ramblas. Try the shops around Mercat de Sant Antoni (recently renovated, great for local products and a Sunday market vibe even on weekdays). Head back to the hotel in Sant Just Desvern to collect luggage. Pack and prepare for departure or onward travel.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in Sant Just Desvern or a final tapas session in the city before heading to the airport or your next destination. If your departure is the following day, enjoy a relaxed evening in the local neighbourhood – grab a cold beer and tapas at a neighbourhood bar and reflect on the trip.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast if included, or a local café near the hotel – coffee and tostada con tomate y aceite for €3–5.
meals.lunch: Mercat de Sant Antoni area – grab a bocadillo or a menú del día for €10–13.
meals.dinner: Local neighbourhood restaurant in Sant Just Desvern or a final menú del día in the city. Budget €12–15 for a satisfying farewell meal with wine.

day_by_day.notes: Budget summary for the 5 days (excluding flights and accommodation): Transport T-Casual card ~€12, Parc Güell ~€10, Sagrada Família ~€28, Palau de la Música ~€25, Montjuïc cable car ~€13, Castell de Montjuïc ~€5, Pavelló Mies van der Rohe ~€5, Monestir de Pedralbes ~€5. Total attractions ~€103. Meals averaging €25–30/day = ~€125–150. Miscellaneous drinks/snacks ~€30. Grand total estimate: €260–290 for 5 days, making it a very achievable budget trip to Barcelona.

day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Barcelona El Prat Airport at 19:20. Take the Aerobus or taxi (~25 min) to Sercotel Porta Barcelona in Sant Just Desvern. Check in, freshen up, and take a relaxed stroll around the local neighbourhood to get oriented. The hotel is near the L3 metro line giving easy access to the city.

meals.lunch: N/A – in transit or airport snack
meals.dinner: Casual dinner close to the hotel: try Restaurant Can Rafel or a local tapas bar in Sant Just Desvern town centre (~10 min walk). Budget €15–22 per person for a menú del día or tapas spread.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light – jet lag and travel fatigue are real. Pick up a T-Casual metro card (10 trips, ~€11.35) at the airport or nearest metro station to save money on transport all week. Weather in August averages 28.9°C so pack light, breathable clothing.

day_by_day.morning: Sagrada Família Guided Tour (09:00–11:30): Take the L3 metro from Zona Universitària to Diagonal, then L5 to Sagrada Família (~30 min from hotel area). Join a guided tour of Gaudí's iconic unfinished basilica to uncover its intricate symbolism, the Nativity and Passion facades, and the breathtaking interior forest of columns. Book tickets in advance online (€26–35 with tower access). Arrive early to beat the August crowds and heat.
day_by_day.afternoon: Gothic Quarter & El Born Architecture Walk (13:00–17:00): After lunch, head to the Gothic Quarter via metro (L5 to Jaume I). Follow a self-guided or small-group walking tour through Barcelona's medieval lanes – the Cathedral of Barcelona, Plaça Reial, the Roman walls, and into the trendy El Born neighbourhood with its modernista iron market (Mercat de Santa Caterina) and boutique-lined streets. Pick up a free map at the tourist office on Plaça de Catalunya.
day_by_day.afternoon_note: Rest at a café during the hottest part of the day (14:00–16:00) – this is very much the local custom.
day_by_day.evening: Explore El Born's bar scene for pre-dinner drinks, then enjoy dinner in the neighbourhood before heading back to the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or a nearby café con leche and croissant (~€4–6). Alternatively, grab a fresh pastry at a local bakery in Sant Just Desvern.
meals.lunch: Bar El Xampanyet in El Born – a classic cava bar with excellent tapas (anchovies, cheese, cured meats). Budget €12–18 per person.
meals.dinner: El Born neighbourhood: try Llamber or Bar del Pla for modern Catalan cuisine. Budget €25–35 per person including wine.

day_by_day.notes: August is peak tourist season – pre-book Sagrada Família tickets at least 2–3 weeks ahead. Wear comfortable walking shoes for the Gothic Quarter cobblestones. Stay hydrated; carry a water bottle.

day_by_day.morning: Pavillon Mies van der Rohe & Montjuïc Architecture Trail (09:30–12:30): Take the L3 metro to Espanya, then walk or take the escalators up to Montjuïc. Begin at the Barcelona Pavilion (Pavelló Mies van der Rohe) – a landmark of modernist architecture built for the 1929 World Exposition, famous for its travertine marble, glass, and the iconic Barcelona Chair. Entry ~€10. Continue along the Montjuïc architecture trail: the Palau Nacional (MNAC), the Grec Theatre, and the Olympic Stadium area, appreciating the grand urban planning of the 1929 and 1992 legacies.
day_by_day.afternoon: Poble Sec Exploration & Rest (13:00–18:00): Descend from Montjuïc into the Poble Sec neighbourhood. Wander Carrer de Blai – Barcelona's famous pintxos street – for a late lunch. Afterwards, return to the hotel for a siesta and pool time (if available) or relax before the evening. This is a good afternoon to recharge before a big night out.
day_by_day.evening: Poble Sec & Montjuïc Nightlife Circuit (20:00 onwards): Return to Poble Sec for the full nightlife experience. Start with dinner at a pintxos bar on Carrer de Blai, then move to cocktail bars like Bar Calders or Bodega Sepúlveda. Later, head to Sala Apolo or Discothèque on Carrer Nou de la Rambla for live music or club nights. Barcelona nightlife starts late – clubs peak after midnight.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a café near the metro – café amb llet and pa amb tomàquet (bread with tomato) is the quintessential Catalan breakfast. ~€5–8.
meals.lunch: Carrer de Blai pintxos bars (Quimet & Quimet or Bar Calders) – graze on pintxos and vermouth. Budget €10–15 per person.
meals.dinner: Dinner at a Poble Sec restaurant before the nightlife circuit – try Bodega Sepúlveda or Tickets (book well ahead) for a special experience. Budget €20–30 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Sala Apolo entry is typically €12–18; check their programme in advance at apolo.com. Wear comfortable but stylish shoes – Barcelona nightlife involves a lot of walking between venues. Last metro back toward Sant Just Desvern runs around 00:00 on weekdays; take a taxi or Cabify after midnight (~€15–20).

day_by_day.morning: Palau de la Música Catalana Daytime Visit & Neighbourhood (10:00–12:30): After a relaxed morning start (recovering from the night before), take the metro to Urquinaona. Visit the Palau de la Música Catalana – a UNESCO World Heritage modernista masterpiece by Lluís Domènech i Montaner. Take a guided tour of the interior (€22) to see the extraordinary stained-glass skylight, ornate ceramic mosaics, and sculpted concert hall. This is one of the most visually stunning buildings in Europe.
day_by_day.afternoon: Eixample Modernisme Walk & Passeig de Gràcia (13:00–18:00): Walk or metro to Passeig de Gràcia to explore the 'Block of Discord' – Casa Batlló (exterior or interior, €35+ if entering), Casa Amatller, and Casa Lleó Morera, all showcasing competing modernista styles. Stroll up to Casa Milà (La Pedrera) for its iconic rooftop (€25 with rooftop access). Window-shop the elegant boulevard and rest at a terrace café during the afternoon heat.
day_by_day.evening: Palau de la Música Catalana Evening Concert (20:00–22:00): Return to the Palau de la Música for a live evening concert – the perfect way to experience this architectural gem in its intended purpose. Check the August programme at palaumusica.cat; tickets range from €18–60 depending on the performance. Dress smart-casual. Afterwards, enjoy a nightcap in the El Born or Eixample bar scene.

meals.breakfast: Sleep in and have a late breakfast – try Federal Café in Sant Antoni or a café near Urquinaona. Avocado toast or eggs with coffee. ~€8–12.
meals.lunch: Cervecería Catalana on Carrer de Mallorca in Eixample – excellent tapas and montaditos in a buzzing mid-range setting. Budget €18–25 per person.
meals.dinner: Pre-concert dinner near the Palau: try Els Quatre Gats (historic modernista café-restaurant) or a Catalan bistro in El Born. Budget €22–32 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Book Palau de la Música concert tickets well in advance – August performances sell out quickly. If budget allows, the Casa Batlló night experience ('Magic Nights') is a spectacular architectural and multimedia show (~€49). Combine the Palau tour in the morning with the concert in the evening for a full modernisme immersion day.

day_by_day.morning: Barceloneta Beach & Waterfront (09:00–12:00): Take the metro to Barceloneta for a morning swim before the beach gets too crowded and hot. Walk along the Passeig Marítim, admire Frank Gehry's golden 'Fish' sculpture, and explore the Port Olímpic marina. This is a relaxed, free morning to soak up Barcelona's coastal side.
day_by_day.afternoon: Gràcia Neighbourhood & Park Güell (13:00–17:30): Head to the charming Gràcia neighbourhood for lunch and a wander through its village-like squares (Plaça del Sol, Plaça de la Vila de Gràcia). Then walk uphill or take a taxi to Park Güell – Gaudí's fantastical park with its mosaic terraces, gingerbread gatehouses, and panoramic city views. Book the Monumental Zone ticket in advance (~€10). The park is best visited in the late afternoon when the light is golden and the heat eases slightly.
day_by_day.evening: Final Evening – Rooftop Bars & Farewell Dinner (19:30 onwards): Enjoy Barcelona's famous rooftop bar culture for sunset drinks. Try La Isabela rooftop at Hotel 1898 on La Rambla, or the Terraza del Claris in Eixample (€10–15 per cocktail). End the trip with a memorable farewell dinner in Eixample or El Born, then head back to the hotel to pack for departure.

meals.breakfast: Barceloneta beach chiringuito (beach bar) – fresh orange juice, croissant, and coffee with a sea view. ~€6–9.
meals.lunch: Gràcia neighbourhood: La Pepita or a local menú del día restaurant – two courses with wine for €13–16 per person. Great value.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner: Bodega Sepúlveda (Poble Sec) or Parking Pizza (Eixample) for something relaxed, or splurge slightly at Moments or a Catalan restaurant in Eixample. Budget €30–45 per person for a special last meal.

day_by_day.notes: Park Güell's Monumental Zone has timed entry – book online to guarantee your slot. August 47.5mm rainfall average means occasional afternoon thunderstorms are possible; carry a light rain layer. Check departure logistics: the Aerobus from Plaça de Catalunya to the airport takes ~35 min and costs €6.75 one-way – factor this into your Day 6 morning if flying out the next day.

meals.dinner: Dinner at Can Cortada (approx. 15 min drive) – a historic 15th-century farmhouse restaurant serving refined Catalan cuisine in a stunning rustic-elegant setting. Perfect first-night introduction to authentic Catalan gastronomy. Reservation strongly recommended.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light – jet lag and travel fatigue are real. Pre-arrange private airport transfer before departure. Confirm hotel check-in details in advance as arrival is after 19:00. Pack light carry-on essentials in case of any luggage delays.

day_by_day.morning: Sagrada Família Guided Tour – Begin the day with a premium guided tour of Gaudí's iconic unfinished basilica. Book a skip-the-line private or small-group tour with tower access for panoramic views over Barcelona. Arrive early (9:00–9:30 AM) to beat the August crowds and experience the morning light streaming through the stained-glass windows in full glory. Your guide will decode the intricate symbolism of the Nativity and Passion facades, the forest-like nave, and Gaudí's sacred geometry. Allow 2–2.5 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Gothic Quarter & El Born Architecture Walk – After lunch, take a private or small-group walking tour through Barcelona's medieval Gothic Quarter and the trendy El Born neighbourhood. Explore the Roman ruins beneath Plaça del Rei, the soaring Barcelona Cathedral, Carrer del Bisbe's neo-Gothic bridge, and the stunning Basílica de Santa Maria del Mar. Transition into El Born's modernista iron market (Mercat de Santa Caterina nearby) and boutique-lined streets. Allow 2.5–3 hours at a leisurely premium pace.
day_by_day.evening: Poble Sec & Montjuïc Nightlife Circuit – Experience Barcelona's vibrant nightlife starting with pre-dinner pintxos and craft vermouth at a curated pintxos bar on Carrer de Blai in Poble Sec. Then ascend to Montjuïc for the Magic Fountain light show (check seasonal schedule – typically Mon & Wed evenings in August). Cap the night at a rooftop bar or a sophisticated cocktail lounge back in the Eixample district.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or nearby Cafè de l'Acadèmia (Gothic Quarter) – artisan pastries, fresh orange juice, and specialty coffee in a charming historic setting.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Cervecería Catalana on Carrer de Mallorca – a Barcelona institution renowned for its premium tapas, fresh seafood, and Catalan small plates. Expect a short wait even with reservations in August.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Bodega Sepúlveda or Quimet & Quimet (standing tapas, legendary) in Poble Sec before the nightlife circuit begins, or opt for a sit-down dinner at Tickets (Albert Adrià's avant-garde tapas restaurant – book weeks in advance).

day_by_day.notes: Book Sagrada Família tickets well in advance – August is peak season and slots sell out fast. Wear comfortable walking shoes for the Gothic Quarter tour. The Magic Fountain schedule varies; verify dates at barcelonaturisme.com. Private transfer or taxi recommended between Sagrada Família and Gothic Quarter.

day_by_day.morning: Pavillon Mies van der Rohe & Montjuïc Architecture Trail – Start the morning with a visit to the iconic Barcelona Pavilion, Mies van der Rohe's minimalist 1929 World Exposition masterpiece – a pilgrimage site for architecture lovers. Admire the interplay of travertine marble, green onyx, and the reflective pool. Continue along the Montjuïc Architecture Trail, visiting the Fundació Joan Miró (architecturally significant, designed by Josep Lluís Sert) and the Palau Nacional (now MNAC), with sweeping views over the city from its terrace. Allow 3–3.5 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Free afternoon for leisure and exploration. Options include: a private visit to Casa Batlló or Casa Milà (La Pedrera) on the Passeig de Gràcia – both Gaudí masterpieces with premium after-hours or rooftop access options. Alternatively, explore the upscale boutiques of Passeig de Gràcia and Avinguda Diagonal, or relax at the hotel pool if available.
day_by_day.evening: Palau de la Música Catalana Evening Concert – Attend a live concert at this UNESCO World Heritage modernista masterpiece designed by Lluís Domènech i Montaner. The stained-glass skylight, sculpted columns, and ornate ceramic details make this one of the world's most breathtaking concert halls. Check the August programme for classical, flamenco, or jazz performances. Dress code: smart elegant. Arrive 30 minutes early to admire the interior before the performance.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Federal Café (Sant Antoni neighbourhood) or hotel breakfast – avocado toast, eggs Benedict, and specialty single-origin coffee.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Parking Pizza or Honest Greens (Eixample) for a lighter, premium midday meal, or splurge at Disfrutar (ranked among the world's best restaurants – advance reservation essential) for a once-in-a-trip tasting menu experience.
meals.dinner: Pre-concert dinner at Casa Leopoldo (El Raval) – a legendary Barcelona institution serving traditional Catalan seafood and market cuisine since 1929, just minutes from the Palau de la Música.

day_by_day.notes: Barcelona Pavilion opens at 10:00 AM – arrive early for the best light and fewest crowds. Book Palau de la Música concert tickets in advance at palaumusica.cat. If visiting Casa Batlló, book the 'Magic Nights' rooftop experience for a premium sunset view. Smart casual attire recommended for the concert.

day_by_day.morning: Park Güell & Gràcia Neighbourhood – Begin with a timed-entry visit to Park Güell, Gaudí's fantastical hilltop park with its mosaic terraces, gingerbread gatehouses, and sweeping panoramic views over Barcelona. Book the Monumental Zone access in advance. Afterwards, descend into the charming Gràcia neighbourhood – a village-within-a-city with modernista architecture, independent boutiques, and lively plazas. Explore Plaça del Sol and Plaça de la Vila de Gràcia at a leisurely pace.
day_by_day.afternoon: Eixample Modernisme Deep Dive – Dedicate the afternoon to Barcelona's golden Eixample grid, the world's greatest concentration of modernista architecture. Visit the interiors of Casa Amatller and Casa Lleó Morera on the 'Block of Discord' (Manzana de la Discordia). If not visited yesterday, secure premium access to La Pedrera (Casa Milà) including the rooftop warrior chimneys and the Espai Gaudí exhibition. Consider a private architecture guide for deeper context.
day_by_day.evening: Upscale Nightlife in Eixample & Sant Gervasi – Begin the evening with cocktails at the rooftop bar of the Hotel Arts or the W Barcelona (beachfront, stunning sunset views). Move on to the Eixample's 'Gayxample' district for vibrant bar-hopping, or head to the exclusive Sutton Club or Opium Barcelona for a premium nightclub experience. Barcelona's nightlife truly begins after midnight.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at La Pepita (Gràcia) – artisan croissants, fresh fruit, and specialty coffee in a beautifully tiled vintage setting.
meals.lunch: Lunch at La Pepita Gràcia or Botafumeiro – a legendary Galician seafood restaurant on Carrer Gran de Gràcia, famous for its percebes (barnacles), oysters, and grilled fish. A true premium Barcelona institution.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Moments (2 Michelin stars, Mandarin Oriental Hotel) – Chef Raül Balam's refined contemporary Catalan cuisine in an elegant setting on Passeig de Gràcia. One of Barcelona's finest dining experiences.

day_by_day.notes: Park Güell Monumental Zone tickets must be booked online in advance – August slots sell out days ahead. Wear sun protection and comfortable shoes for the uphill walk. La Pedrera's 'La Pedrera de Nit' evening rooftop experience (with live music) is available in summer – highly recommended as an alternative evening activity. Nightclubs have a dress code; smart-casual to elegant attire required.

day_by_day.morning: Barceloneta & Port Olímpic Waterfront – Spend a relaxed final morning at the Barceloneta beachfront. Opt for a private sailing or yacht charter from Port Olímpic for a 2-hour morning cruise along the Barcelona coastline – a premium way to see the city from the sea, with views of the Sagrada Família skyline, Montjuïc, and the W Hotel sail. Alternatively, visit the Aquàrium de Barcelona or simply enjoy a leisurely walk along the Passeig Marítim.
day_by_day.afternoon: El Born Cultural & Memorial Centre & Final Shopping – Visit the El Born Cultural Centre (housed in a stunning 19th-century iron market) to see the preserved ruins of the 1714 siege of Barcelona. Explore the surrounding El Born streets for premium shopping – artisan jewellery, design objects, and fashion. Head to Passeig de Gràcia for luxury brand shopping (Loewe, Massimo Dutti flagship, Custo Barcelona) before returning to the hotel to pack and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Dinner & Departure Preparation – Enjoy a memorable farewell dinner before arranging a private transfer back to the airport or onward destination. Alternatively, if the flight is the following day, spend the evening at a sophisticated rooftop bar for a final toast to Barcelona.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or at La Mar Salada (Barceloneta) – a premium seafood restaurant steps from the beach, serving excellent brunch with fresh Mediterranean produce.
meals.lunch: Lunch at El Xiringuito Escribà (Barceloneta beach) – a legendary beachside restaurant by the Escribà pastry dynasty, serving premium paella, fideuà, and fresh seafood with your feet practically in the sand.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Enoteca Paco Pérez (Hotel Arts, 2 Michelin stars) – an extraordinary Mediterranean fine-dining experience with impeccable wine pairings, overlooking the sea. The perfect final Barcelona memory.

day_by_day.notes: Book the yacht charter at least 48 hours in advance through the hotel concierge or a luxury experience provider like Luxury Barcelona or Context Travel. El Xiringuito Escribà is extremely popular in August – reserve a table for lunch well in advance. Confirm private airport transfer timing based on your departure flight. Allow extra time for August traffic on the return to the airport.

query: Barcelona architecture and nightlife, $2000, 5 days, August from NYC
